#3702. ‘The name’s Cullen. Edward Cullen’: Robert Pattinson reportedly top choice for next James Bond

It'll be exciting to see how he pulls it off if selected.

Bond. James Bond. Two words. Two syllables. Sharp, striking, piercing your chest as soon as they are uttered. They mean a lot to many, and every so often they are thrown into the ether, like a phonetic parasite seeking their next host. Who will carry them for the next year, two, five, a decade? A hard question to answer.

But according to a new rumor, Robert Pattinson is the top choice to embody Ian Fleming’s womanizer spy, with Amazon MGM reportedly considering him their favorite for the role. As first reported by Matthew Belloni in Puck (via The Guardian), Pattinson was given “favorable contract terms” to play this legendary character, which would see him star in three movies rather than the four expected of other candidates. The actor would also be paid significantly more, which signals how keen Amazon MGM is to get his face and name associated with the brand and character.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Previously, it was claimed Callum Turner was in the running for Bond going forward, according to Deadline, with Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor also putting themselves up. That outlet did say four offers were sent out but managed to confirm just these three, and it would appear now that Pattinson was the ultimate contender.

Now, if you asked me, I’d say Turner was, at least in terms of physical appearance and stature (which, of course, is almost just as important as actual acting skills for a character like James Bond) suits the character much more than Pattinson. The latter practically kills every role involving strange, mysterious, and at times evidently neurodivergent characters, and while he did nail the strong, silent stoic in 2022’s The Batman, I still fail to see how he could handle a highly sexualized, outgoing, womanizer Bond.

However, Daniel Craig’s Bond was markedly different than what we were used to. He had a lot more depth and a broad, emotionally charged backstory that fundamentally altered how he behaved. The core tenets of the character remained intact, though Craig did give them somewhat of a sociopathic tone.

How Pattinson will play the character and what flair he will end up giving him remains to be seen, but I’m confident enough in his acting skills to believe just enough that he can actually pull it off.

In the lead up to GTA 6's long-awaited launch, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has called out companies like Anthropic and OpenAI for allowing users to plagiarize and clone pre-existing games using generative AI.

Generative AI's usage in game development has been highly controversial for many reasons, but in recent months, AI copycats have become an increasingly prevalent issue. Some Steam developers even cancelled demos or playtests out of fear their games would be cloned and put up for sale before their official release dates. Copycats of popular games like Mecca Chameleon can sometimes flood the storefront in no time, too.

"I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," Zelnick says when asked if he'd like to see more AI companies restrict users from reverse engineering games, in an interview with IGN.

"And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he adds.

Anthropic recently added a new rule to Claude's backend code to block users from "recreating someone else's specific game," after lots of developers essentially had their work ripped off in mere minutes. The restriction might also stop Claude from being used in the tidal wave of vibe-coded recompilations we've seen in recent months - Mario Kart Wii, Banjo-Tooie and The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening included.

"Using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy," Anthropic's member of technical staff Addy Osmani said at the time. "Original games, genre games, and games built from your own designs and assets are meant to keep working."

ChatGPT owner OpenAI seemingly has no such restrictions in place for now.

#3699. New York City, Mayor Mamdani to host youth game dev contest to help boost local game industry growth

The home locale of Rockstar Games’ corporate headquarters is trying to invest in further game development locally, thanks in large part to a certain popular mayor and his office.

Today, New York City and Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced NYC Game Jam, a two-day youth competition for game development in which young New Yorkers “design and build a video game around a set theme,” according to a report by Variety. It will take place this weekend.

But don’t expect a return to Liberty City here. The competition’s theme is “Get There Already,” focused on the city’s transit, and according to the Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment, “participants will build a game about getting across the city” and “every game must be about transit or the experience of getting around a city, suitable for all ages, and free of violence, weapons, and other illicit activity.” No grand theft here.

The office also said that NYC’s gaming sector lists “about 7,900 jobs across approximately 380 firms and generates $2.6 billion in annual economic impact,” so this competition is an effort to continue that trend and keep games being developed in the city.

“Whether you’re exploring the forests of Hyrule or riding across the frontier at Nuevo Paraíso, video games invite us into worlds born from the imagination of their designers. And that creativity represents an enormous opportunity here in New York City,” Mamdani said. “As the industry grows, we want to make sure the next generation of game developers and designers can build their futures right here at home. This Game Jam is a chance to open the door to that industry for young New Yorkers, connect them with the people shaping it, and give them the tools and support to turn their biggest ideas into careers.”

A panel of industry veterans will select three finalists in the contest, with first place winning $3,000, second place $1,500, and third place $500, with the winnings to be split amongst all members of the game-making teams. It’s unclear if generative AI will be allowed in the contest.

As a native New Yorker, this excites me. I’d love more studios to work out of Manhattan rather than California, selfishly, because it’s less travel for me.

TSMC, the juggernaut that produces roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips, has discovered a data leak said to contain over 46,000 employee records, according to Seeking Alpha.

The company made a Form 6-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday, stating: "TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization. Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised."

The company says the info has been verified to match data "stored in the system services of a cloud service provider," although said provider is not named. TSMC says it has informed those impacted by the breach and is providing support, and has also engaged with the cloud service vendor, investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency to "ascertain the facts and take necessary actions."

Taiwanese outlet United Daily News reports that hackers were allegedly offering the employee records on an underground forum for the princely sum of three bitcoin, in exchange for 6.9 GB worth of private data.

The outlet also says that, "according to information online" (via machine translation), hackers were also selling what appears to be TSMC employee data on other forums, releasing a small sample which is said to contain a vast array of personal details, including national ID numbers, addresses, and banking information.

TSMC has confirmed in its statement that the leaked data is unrelated to the company's operations, or customer-related information.

This isn't the first time TSMC has been in the headlines in relation to cybersecurity. Back in 2023, ransomware outfit LockBit attempted to extort the company for $70 million after a claimed hack.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

TSMC denied it had been directly hacked, revealing in a statement that IT hardware supplier Kinmax Technology had been the victim of a "cybersecurity incident" instead, which "led to the leak of information pertinent to server initial setup and configuration." Kinmax also released a statement at the time confirming the breach.

Being such a large and wealthy company at the heart of the tech supply chain, it's no surprise that hackers are keen to gain any details on TSMC if they can. In both these cases, it seems that TSMC's own systems remained secure, but an outside party may have let the side down.

Regardless, I doubt it's the last major data leak I'll be writing about before 2026 is out. This year has been characterised by cybersecurity incidents left, right and centre, and in this every-more-interconnected world, it seems even some of the most security-conscious companies are far from immune.

Scrooge's biggest problem might be convincing us to watch another Christmas Carol.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Johnny Depp is returning to Hollywood in a big way with Ebenezer, and considering everything that's happened in his career over the last several years, I've been curious to see how audiences respond. The actor is playing one of literature's most famously unpleasant characters in a new adaptation of A Christmas Carol, which arrives on the 2026 movie schedule this Friday. But apparently some theater executives aren't particularly worried about Depp being the reason people stay home.

According to Variety, theater owners are cautiously optimistic about the holiday movie, which marks Depp's first major Hollywood studio film in eight years. Based on the first look at his transformation into Ebenezer Scrooge, he's clearly embracing the character's unpleasant side. While his return certainly comes with some baggage, Regal CEO Eduardo Acuña thinks the actor and the material are a pretty natural fit. He explained:

I’m optimistic for a few reasons. Even though this story predates him, it feels like the character was written for Johnny Depp. And it’s good IP from a very distinctive filmmaker.

I have to agree with him about the casting. The Edward Scissorhands star has spent much of his time on screen playing eccentric characters who aren't always particularly pleasant company. Between Willy Wonka, the Mad Hatter and Captain Jack Sparrow, the man has practically built a career out of making weirdos entertaining. Playing Ebenezer Scrooge seems right up his alley.

Then there's director Ti West, whose work on X, Pearl and MaXXXine makes me especially curious about what he'll do with Charles Dickens' ghosts. He's had some serious praise for the actor's take on Scrooge, which only makes me more interested in seeing the finished movie. The filmmaker has leaned into the story's supernatural elements, and I've already been impressed by how much personality Depp brings to the character in the trailers.

Of course, the bigger conversation involves whether moviegoers are willing to embrace the 21 Jump Street breakout again. His career was significantly affected by his legal battles with ex-wife Amber Heard, including allegations of domestic abuse and their highly publicized defamation trial in 2022. Since then, he's worked primarily on smaller international projects, including Jeanne du Barry. We recently covered how one of that film's producers believes Depp is poised for a Hollywood comeback, and if theater operators are right, his past controversies might play a smaller role in Ebenezer's box office performance than some expect.

Classic Cinemas CEO Chris Johnson told the outlet that the bigger question is whether audiences find this particular adaptation compelling. After all, we've seen Scrooge countless times before, from Alastair Sim's 1951 performance to Bill Murray's wonderfully ridiculous turn in Scrooged. Disney even spent about $200 million to bring Jim Carrey's animated version to theaters in 2009.

There's also the matter of money. According to reports, Ebenezer cost approximately $38 million to produce, with another $50 million spent on marketing. Depp reportedly accepted a $5 million salary, considerably less than the enormous paychecks he commanded during his Pirates of the Caribbean years, which could help explain Paramount's relatively cautious approach.

The movie is currently tracking toward a $20 million domestic opening weekend, with another $20 million expected overseas. Those aren't Pirates numbers, but nobody seems to be expecting them, either.

Personally, I think the executives make a fair point. There are only so many ways to tell A Christmas Carol, and audiences have plenty of versions to revisit every December. Depp's name will undoubtedly get people talking, but whether they recommend this particular adaptation afterward is another matter. At least his co-stars seem confident they've made something worthwhile. Rupert Grint previously praised his performance, while suggesting that West's take on the familiar story offers something different.

Ebenezer opens in theaters Nov. 13. I'm curious to see whether West and the former leading man can make an old Christmas ghost story feel fresh again. And if audiences don't show up, I suspect Hollywood will have plenty to argue about besides the man playing Scrooge.

#3696. Monster Hunter Wilds' upcoming Ascendance expansion may be getting a beta, some curious Steam backend updates suggest

Monster Hunter Wilds's first expansion, Ascendance, is set for release sometime next year. But, judging by some very suspect recent changes to the Wilds beta app on Steam, we may be playing some of the new stuff earlier than we thought.

On Steam, Capcom quietly updated the Monster Hunter Wilds Beta app to now say Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test. You can see the change log on SteamDB (via PC Gamer), which also shows an updated key art - all signs that point towards an impending beta for Ascendance.

The beta app is the same one those who played the original Wilds beta had in their library. Though the app was removed following the beta's conclusion, because the two share the same ID, the beta should be visible in users' list of played games under the new name. This could mean players won't need to sign up for the supposed Ascendance beta, seemingly only needing to download the new client.

Seeing as Ascendance itself doesn't have a release date, beyond a nebulous 2027 target, it's hard to speculate when Capcom plans to release the beta. Sometime early in 2027 would be a good guess, perhaps alongside a release date announcement.

Capcom has shown off Ascendance on multiple occasions, more recently in Sony's September State of Play, where we got to see a number of the expansion's new features. A few days later at Tokyo Game Show, we got a first look at returning Elder Dragon Teostra, which we can hunt in the expansion.

Capcom is keen for Ascendance to deliver the level of challenge Monster Hunter is known for, following feedback that the launch version of Wilds simply lacked that expected level of difficulty. While post-launch updates have certainly raised the level of challenge, Ascendance looks to be the next step up.

#3695. Cities: Skylines 2 goes free-to-play, but only for a limited time

Cities: Skylines 2, Paradox Interactive’s ambitious follow-up to one of the best city builders of all time, has gone free-to-play. However, this will only apply for this weekend, with the event closing in the afternoon hours of Nov. 16.

The free-to-play model has more than doubled the game’s concurrent player count, bumping it from about 8,000 to over 16,000, according to SteamDB. People seem genuinely interested in checking the game out, though its less-than-stellar reviews and horrible reputation still seem to impact players’ willingness to actually spend any money on it, despite numerous discounts.

Speaking of which, Cities: Skylines 2 is also 30 percent off, or more if you go for the bundle and already own the original.

Ever since its original creators, Colossal Order, gave the game up to Paradox Interactive and Iceflake Studios, the game has gradually improved in overall quality. Things are undoubtedly moving at a snail’s pace, with Iceflake doing as much as it possibly can to salvage the title and reclaim some of that lost trust from the players. Despite their best efforts and, of course, several DLC releases, Cities: Skylines 2 still has a “mixed” rating on Steam, meaning it cannot be featured on the store’s front page or get any of that juicy free exposure from Valve.

The recent reviews fare much better, though. With 72 percent of those being positive, Cities 2 thus holds a “mostly positive” rating in this category, but players still have a lot of bones to pick with the game’s many systems, namely traffic and simulation, whereby bugs and issues that’ve been there from the start remain in the game.

I, for one, was extremely excited to get into Cities 2 ahead of its original release in 2023. The original Cities: Skylines is one of my favorite games of all time, and certainly my favorite city builder, and its sequel promised to up the ante on so many different levels. I was chiefly enamored by how detailed the new assets were in Cities 2, how big everything was, and how that would allow me to zoom in and see the minutiae from up close, but my hype evaporated once I got my hands on it.

The jank was unbearable, and the faulty simulation meant the game lied to you all the time, feeding you false information to make it seem like simulation was happening when, in fact, it was all fake.

Iceflake has since fixed many of these issues, and I will definitely be revisiting the game in the coming days.

#3692. World of Warcraft: Forever secret hunters have found the MMO's first hidden treasure

World of Warcraft secret hunters are a noble breed, known for scouring the MMO for years for hidden trinkets and treasures. With World of Warcraft: Forever's launch, they've uncovered a quest chain for an especially fancy sword.

Over the past week, members of the WoW Secret Hunters Discord found a quest chain that takes place entirely on the Zephras Isle, meaning you'll need to have access to the Skyborne elves to grab this sword. Navigating the island, you'll need to first pick up an ancient heirloom ring from the starting zone. Simple enough!

Then, you'll need to head to Duskwood to gather the Night Watchman's Torch, a handy light source primarily used to light up areas across the darkened woods near Stormwind. It turns out this torch has uses far beyond this one zone however, as taking it back to the Ruins of Ban'aethal on the Zephras Isle will reward you with a secret quest and the Ancient Hilt.

With the hilt and ring, you then must track down an Ancient Blade from one of several spawn locations on the Zephras Isle. Once you finally track it down, that's the end of part one of this quest chain. You get the sword: Eluvi'ana, which on its own isn't particularly strong, but is speculated to be upgraded later down the line.

You then need to get a corrupted water globe from either Darkshore or the Blackfathom Deeps dungeon depending on your faction, do a fetch quest for a hidden spirit in Ashenvale, then take your hoard of special quest items to a NPC in the new Shen'Dralar zone.

He won't give you the finished sword. Instead he sends you to gather more items from higher-level zones. You'll need to raid a secluded vault in Feralas that you can only see with the Ancient Hilt, dive underwater in Azshara, and kill Highborne Shades in Winterspring. Once you've done all that, you can then cleanse the orb up in Hyjal, speak to the fella back in Shen'Dralar, then shimmy over to the end game Dire Maul dungeon to speak to Prince Tortheldrin about *another* sword.

This is how far the World of Warcraft: Forever secret hunter community has gotten to. It's believed that grinding up the Shen'dralar reputation to Honoured is required for the next step, as Prince Tortheldrin pretty much says as much in his dialogue. So the hunt is still on!

These sorts of secrets make up an important part of any good MMO: the solving of mysteries in these vast digital open worlds. In retail WoW, I have fond memories of the Waist of Time quest chain, which was an arduous and comical grind for a fancy belt during the Battle for Azeroth expansion. This secret sword quest chain may very well evolve into something as legendary as that, at least I hope so!

If you're not already playing it, World of Warcraft: Forever is plenty of fun. A record-breaking number of players are making the journey through Azeroth right now, diving into quests and dungeons new and old.

While the ‘90s are pretty trendy in pop culture right now, it’s been quite a long time since the decades stars were household names. Only, if you were to ask Boy Meets World’s Will Friedle, he was never, ever a household name. He says people have never once recognized him in Hollywood, even at the height of his most popular show's fame.

This was true in the ‘90s. It was true in the early aughts. It was true when Girl Meets World was pitched, and brought the classic TGIF series back into the limelight and he made appearances. It’s still true now that Danielle Fishel, Friedle and fellow cast member Ryder Strong host “Pod Meets World,” a podcast about their early fame experiences. Here’s what he had to say.

We always joke about it, but it’s 100% true. I never get recognized. Ever. I mean to a comical point. … One of the things we would do is wherever we’re traveling together, I always take the pictures of Danielle with the fans. So, they’ll go, ‘Will you take a picture of us together?’ I’ll go, ‘Sure, no problem.’ I take a picture.

This happens everywhere. On the streets. At professional events. Will Friedle even said on the Zach Sang Show he and a bunch of Boy Meets World cast members were on a plane and the flight attendant recognized everyone. Well, everyone but one: Will Friedle. The flight attendant gushed about loving each cast member, until Will walked up and the flight attendant just went, ‘Have a good day.’ Brutal.

I’d have trouble believing this, only I saw it happen while watching a live event once, and it’s one the actor also remembers.

A few months ago, I was watching an early Raw event on Netflix and Danielle Fishel was in attendance. That’s not really weird. She’s a noted WWE fan, and I’d seen her around before. This time, though, she’d come with Will Friedle. Smackdown and Raw will often point out celebrities in attendance. So, it wasn’t a surprise when the camera panned to them and was like, “Hey, here’s Boy Meets World star Danielle Fishel.” What was a surprise? They did it without ever once mentioning her co-star was directly next to her.

I remember commenting about it to my husband at the time, and per Friedle himself, it was a deeply cringe moment.

Later that week, we went to the opening of the WWE [Raw] on Netflix. And we had the greatest seats ever. They’re like, ‘We’d like you to come to the front row. We’ll do your little wave.’ And so, they cut to the thing and there’s Danielle and I like [waving] and underneath it says ‘Danielle Fishel.’ Under me? Nothing.

He’s just one of the out of focus guys! Seriously, though, Fishel is a noted WWE fan and has been at events fairly often. Fans recognize her as a notable WWE fan, so in the company’s defense, I can see why she was pointed out over Friedle, who had to be reminded by Fishel in this same interview that the event they were at was a Raw event. She’s the fan. He was the plus one in that case.

To also note, we've even seen the WWE ignore Fishel before in favor of Travis Barker and Kourtney Kardashian, so this is something that happens a fair amount.

Honestly, though, Friedle has a pretty good attitude about this. He says he got to do the whole fame thing, he has a cool career doing something he’s “loved,” and he gets to walk around and “go anywhere” without being hassled in a way his co-stars usually cannot. Fishel and Strong were surprised when Friedle admitted this was true even in the ‘90s and early 2000s, but I do think he has the right attitude about it.

Those who were huge fans were really into the Eric plotline, particularly during the college years, but your average person would think of Corey, Topanga, maybe Mr. Feeny, maybe Shawn Hunter when Boy Meets World came up. Still, I just want to let you know Will, I did see you at the WWE event, and I did recognize you.

Storm's reworked legendary skin will be here for Christmas.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Skin distribution seems to be an issue in pretty much any game with more than one hero and clear favourites. Marvel Rivals has come under fire for it for a while now, ever since players got wise to which heroes were favourites and which had clearly been shoved to the side.

It all came to a head a few months ago when the summer skins were released, and it was revealed that Storm was the only female hero to not get a legendary costume among all the swimsuit designs. Players did not look upon this favourably, as Storm is a hugely popular character and had already gone a long time without the same kind of legendary skins as other heroes like Luna Snow and had been passed over for skins in the Disco and Egyptian God skin lines.

But all the player complaints seem to have gotten through to NetEase, with creative director Guangyun Chen acknowledging in a dev diary that "season 10 has been a challenging one for us." Not only were players upset about only one hero being released this season, but the devs have "been closely following the community's feedback regarding certain heroes receiving fewer costumes. With strong demands for more high-quality Legendary costumes featuring recolours and ultimate ability visual upgrades."

The decision has since been made to upgrade Storm's summer skin to legendary tier with the devs "targeting a release around Christmas this December" for it. Other slightly forgotten heroes who will be getting some visual upgrades include Human Torch, who will get a legendary costume in early December which includes "recolours and ultimate ability VFX". Cloak and Dagger will also be getting a (presumably Valentines Day-themed) skin in February.

"We've been hard at work at this for almost eight months," Guangyun Chen says. "Cloak's design will include full legs. We fully re-animated Cloak's entire movement set strictly for this, we really hope you enjoy it."

But with all these new redesigns and costumes on the way, Guangyun Chen wants to remind players that skins can't just be made or changed at a moment's notice: "Please understand that art asset production requires a certain lead time and simply can't be done overnight. Generally, a single costume takes eight to 10 months to produce from start to finish."

Storm's redesigned summer skin has been in the works for three months already, with the finished product coming out after five months of work. That's under the average of eight to 10 months, but this sounds like the exception not the rule.

#3689. Viva Las Vegas, baby: Rainbow Six reportedly set to return to its high-rolling heights

Call up your buddies, set aside some cash, and get ready to leave it all at the craps tables: Rainbow Six is reportedly heading back to Vegas, baby, Vegas.

According to Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson, three new projects are now in the works at Ubisoft Montreal, and one of them is a new release in the Rainbow Six: Vegas franchise, which last had an entry way back in 2008.

Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six: Vegas launched in 2006 on PC, PS3, Xbox 360, and even the PSP, and Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six: Vegas 2 followed two years later. In the years since, Ubisoft has launched Rainbow Six Siege and its spin-off Rainbow Six Extraction, along with several mobile games, the re-launch of Rainbow Six Siege X, and next year’s turn-based Rainbow Six Tactics.

Henderson says it’s currently unclear what the game will be, but sources state the new project codenamed “Spades” is “likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake, but only time will tell.” Even still, I think a remastered Vegas or Vegas 2 would be cause for excitement in some areas of the internet. He also said one of the other two games at Ubisoft Montreal is another title in the Rainbow universe, so Ubisoft seems to be doubling down and betting big on Rainbow.

The Vegas games followed the Rainbow team dispatched into Las Vegas, Nevada to battle terrorists, featuring a singleplayer campaign and competitive multiplayer that ended up on Major League Gaming’s Pro Circuit.

A return to the Vegas strip would likely be welcome news to many fans, as the Vegas games are regarded by many to be some of the best tactical FPS shooters from their era. I have a friend who I know will be particularly excited, as he was an avid Vegas player who tried to get me to join many times way back when.

#3688. As of this week, PlayStation 5 has surpassed 100 million consoles sold

PlayStation 5 has officially surpassed 100m consoles sold, Sony's updated sales data revealed. The milestone was reached on 10th November, almost exactly six years on from the console's launch.

The figure represents 'sell-in' units, meaning those shipped to retailers, as opposed to 'sell-through' which tracks consoles actually sold to consumers. In other words, the number of PS5s in people's homes is smaller than that 100m.

Nevertheless, this is an impressive achievement, and gets the PS5 ever closer to the PS4's 117m, which it achieved by June 2022. It also means the PS5 has almost matched the original PlayStation in units sold (102.4m). As impressive as the numbers are, historical data shows that PS5 sales have been in decline.

Sony hasn't shied away from discussing that fact in its earnings reports. 2.6m PS5 consoles were sold during the most recent quarter (Q2 of FY2026), well below the 4m sold over the same period the year prior. In fact, Q2 of FY2026 is the lowest second quarter on record in terms of units sold since the PS5's launch.

However, it's also worth noting that, small though it may be, the second quarter's result is higher than the first quarter's 1.6m, the second-lowest of any single quarter since the PS5's launch, beaten only by Q4 of FY2025's 1.5m.

If numbers don't recover in the third and fourth quarters, this may be the PS5's lowest year ever in terms of units sold. Although the second quarter's sales boost can be attributed to the high anticipation of Grand Theft Auto 6, the overall downturn is largely due to the console's higher price; Sony raised the PS5 and PS5 Pro's prices on several occasions since 2020. The company's bottom line, however, hasn't been affected much, as its plan to generate more revenue from its already-engaged audience continues to work.

The wait for GTA 6 is even more astounding when you remember how things used to be

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Game development has changed substantially since the '90s. Hit games were often assembled by small teams in a couple of years – sometimes months – and you'd often see new entries in major franchises every single year. For a 12-year span from 1997 through 2009, that's exactly how the Grand Theft Auto series was, which throws the 13-year wait for GTA 6 into sharp relief.

These days, Rockstar encompasses many studios around the world, but lead development on the GTA series is handled by Rockstar North. The Edinburgh, Scotland studio was once known as DMA Design, and it was under that name that it released the first three Grand Theft Auto games. The first entry launched in 1997, and the sequel followed in 1999.

Those early top-down entries were moderate successes, but GTA as we know it wouldn't arrive until Grand Theft Auto 3. Its massive, 3D open world was a revelation in 2001, and the game became an industry-defining hit. Other publishers started chasing its open-world design and M-rated appeal in the years that followed.

DMA itself became Rockstar North, and the follow-ups were nonstop. Vice City in 2002. San Andreas in 2004. British studio Mobius Entertainment came under the banner, transforming into Rockstar Leeds and creating the PSP spin-offs, Liberty City Stories and Vice City Stories, in 2005 and 2006. Rockstar North released GTA 4 in 2008, and a pair of expansions that were eventually put together as the standalone Episodes from Liberty City in 2009.

That's a total of 10 games released in a 12-year span. The gap between GTA releases would soon expand dramatically. It would be four years before GTA 5 finally hit. And, incredibly, it's been a whopping 13 years between the releases of GTA 5 and GTA 6. Rockstar has, admittedly, filled the gap with the incredible Red Dead Redemption 2 – but it was also developing non-GTA titles at a far more prolific rate in the series' heyday.

The issue of protracted development cycles leading to interminable waits between series entries is hardly unique to Rockstar, and other developers are often paying the price. Final Fantasy's Naoki Yoshida reckons that the long wait between games is making it harder for younger players to connect with the series.

Of course, it doesn't seem like the GTA 6 hype has died down at all because of the 13-year wait – if anything, the gap has helped the anticipation get even bigger. But the prolific release schedule through the '00s helped make the series an institution in the first place, and it's a reminder of just how much the game industry has changed in the past few decades.

#3686. "I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released" - former Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada trashes Microsoft's console in front of senior Xbox staff

Katsuhiro Harada, formerly director on the Tekken series, is known for not pulling his punches. This truth was reinforced recently, as he said he wished the Xbox Series S "wouldn't be released" at a developer panel. All while a member of the Xbox team was in the room.

Per Inven Global, Harada was sitting on a panel at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 in South Korea. The panel was moderated by former Sony president Shuhei Yoshida, and featured Shift Up CTO DongKi Lee (Stellar Blade), Too Kyo Games CEO Kazutaka Kodaka (Dangenrompa), CD Projekt Red associate game director Paweł Sasko (Cyberpunk 2077), Ludeon Studios CEO Tynan Sylvester (Rimworld), and of course CEO of the newly formed VS Studio Katsuhiro Harada (Tekken).

The panel were asked about the advantages of console development, as well as specific challenges when creating games for certain platforms. Harada led the charge, speaking to the advantages consoles provide for fighting game developers, as the hardware is ideal for tournaments and esports events. Following this, he took an opportunity to speak about a console that drew his ire.

"That said, there's something I really want to say while I have the floor. Since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released," Harada said (translations to English via Inven Global). Harada then asked Sasko from the CD Projekt Red team whether he was "upset inside" because of the Xbox Series S.

Sasko proceeded to "burst out laughing" according to Inven Global, before responding: "It constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly."

Harada followed up with additional thoughts: "You just used a very polite and elegant way to say "Xbox Series S sucks," right? (laughs) Low memory is an issue, but the hardest part is that it's a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance. When porting to Switch 2, developers can shift their mindset to 'Switch 2 is a distinct device for Nintendo fans!' But with Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child.

"Furthermore, in markets like the US, there are more Series S users than Series X users, so we can't just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking 'Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?'"

Sasko stepped up to offer some perks to the Series S. While he agreed that many players the full technical context behind the Series S' weaknesses, he pointed out that optimisation for weaker hardware like the Series S made games run "significantly better" across all platforms. He even had a Cyberpunk 2077 example, as optimisation work done for the Switch 2 version were applied to all platforms "to great effect". Sasko also pointed to the affordability side of the argument, saying that the cheaper price of the Series S allows for market expansion.

Harada responded: "Director Paweł packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along. I'm worried they'll feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs)."

Here, Shift Up's DongKi Lee ended the topic with some optimism for Microsoft's future consoles: "Personally, I am looking forward to the next-gen Xbox 'Helix'. From an engineer's standpoint, if you provide us with a dev kit first in Korea as early as possible, we will put in our best efforts to develop for it."

Earlier this year Harada founded Vs Studio with SNK's support, with other veterans from Bandai Namco's Tekken team hopping on board for whatever it's working on. As for the Xbox Helix consoles, in this current hardware environment with bloated costs for RAM and other components, it's reportedly looking a tad expensive. Maybe a Series S equivalent is on the cards?

"If you want to make a videogame like Grand Theft Auto, you need animators, you need musicians, you need so many people from across the creative industries to make them work. And why shouldn't it be our children in our communities who get the chance to get those jobs?"

It's fascinating how things change. I. for instance, used to love staying up all night playing videogames; now I get mad at the world if I miss my bedtime by 10 minutes. In kind of a similar vein, Grand Theft Auto was once the poster child for everything insidious, dangerous, and downright wrong about videogames, but now we have a member of the UK government—a secretary of state, no less—talking about how the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 is something the whole country should be proud of.

"My love for videogames knows no bounds, and I am an avid addict of things like Animal Crossing and the Mario series," Lisa Nandy, the UK's secretary of state for digital, culture, media, and sport, told The Rundown. "I'm not sure I get away with taking a day off to do it, but I think it's something that we can be really proud of.

"One of the reasons that we're investing in arts and music and all of those things that give people the chance to live richer, larger lives is because we are creating jobs in these incredible industries. And if you want to make a videogame like Grand Theft Auto, you need animators, you need musicians, you need so many people from across the creative industries to make them work. And why shouldn't it be our children in our communities who get the chance to get those jobs?"

I'm as politically cynical as most folks, and sure, Nandy is using the moment opportunistically to promote her government—although, cynicism notwithstanding, I do respect her ability to stay on-message by turning a softball question about GTA 6 into talking about job creation.

At the same time, though, this is a remarkable turnaround from, say, 20 years ago, when everyone in a position of authority lost their minds over the Hot Coffee mod for GTA: San Andreas. Some of you might not be old enough to remember (you have no idea how much it pains me to say that) but referring to GTA as a legitimate cultural export in the early 2000s would've got any mainstream Western politician laughed out of the room—and suggesting that it'd be cool if the children (the children!) grew up to make more games like that? Pure political suicide.

As PC Gamer's Evan Lahti wrote in 2017, "Any American who played games in the '90s remembers the period of pearl-clutching and pseudoscientific fear-mongering from senators like Joe Lieberman, who led a call to ban violent videogames." This was serious stuff back then, and it wasn't really until the US Supreme Court ruled that videogames, like other creative works, are protected speech under the First Amendment that the hysteria and hand-wringing started to meaningfully die down.

But now here we are, 15 years later: The Miami Heat are cosplaying as a Vice City sports team, Rockstar is holding a huge GTA music festival featuring Cardi B and Travis Scott, half the state of Florida is embracing a Leonida transformation (and the cops aren't even mad about it), and now we've got the UK government saying it's all quite grand—splendid, even. Time, man. It really is a river carving the bedrock of our souls.

What does someone have to do to land themselves on the list for a Christmas Cruise Cake?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Somehow, one of the things we all seem to know about Tom Cruise is that he likes to send cake to a lot of people during the holiday season. The gift of what is said to be a delicious white chocolate coconut cake has become legendary, as various A-listers have publicly gushed about being recipients for decades. No matter how well-known a celebrity you are, if you got the Cruise Christmas Cake, you’d want everyone to know about it too.

And if you’ve worked with Tom Cruise and never gotten one of those cakes, you’d probably be at least a little bit salty about it. As “Desk Clerk” in Stanley Kubrick’s final film Eyes Wide Shut, Scottish actor Alan Cumming played, you guessed it, a hotel desk clerk who shared a brief but memorable three-minute scene with Cruise’s character, Dr. William Harford, as he searched for an individual who had already checked out. And apparently that just wasn’t enough to land him on the list to receive a cake. Watch the host of The Traitors, currently on the 2026 TV schedule, get all up in his feelings in this clip from The Graham Norton Show:

A post shared by BBC iPlayer (@bbciplayer)

From Top Gun: Maverick co-star Glen Powell to Mission: Impossible star Hayley Atwell and recent Digger scene partner Riz Ahmed, if you’ve worked with Tom Cruise, you’re likely on his list to receive a coconut cake. And it doesn’t seem to matter how long ago you’ve shared the screen. Just ask Kirsten Dunst, who has gotten the cake annually since working alongside one of the biggest movie stars in the world on Interview with the Vampire over 30 years ago.

Because of all this, I can absolutely empathize with Cumming for feeling some kind of way about never having received the coveted coconut cake that’s become as famous as the actor who gifts it. It also makes me curious about who else is on this no-cake list. But I think the funniest thing about all of this is that Alan Cumming revealed that, even if he did receive the coconut bundt, he likely wouldn’t even be able to eat it. While on The Graham Norton Show, he had this to say to Severance star and fellow guest Tramell Tillman, himself a cake recipient:

[I] never got a bloody cake, no… Listen I’m vegan, so probably I wouldn’t be able to have it.

Even though he admits that he can’t actually even eat the cake, the Toy Story 5 voice actor seems particularly bothered by the volume of coconut bundts that are sent out. If it were a very selective, very small group of recipients, it could soften the blow of hurt feelings for not getting one yourself. But I’m only aware of any of this myself because of how often it’s talked about and how many different people reveal they’re a part of this Cruise Cake Club. Apparently, even Graham Norton himself made it onto the list, which Cumming learned in real time while on the talk show. He said:

He must send out thousands of cakes. Maybe I just watch your show a lot, but it seems that everybody on your show has got a cake from Tom Cruise. Did you get one too? Bitch. Why Tom, why?! Why am I not getting a cake?

I don’t know if any of this pleading will get the Emmy Award-winning host and his iconic fashion choices any closer to receiving a coconut cake (or a vegan replacement) from Tom Cruise, but I’m rooting for him. I also hope, if he ever does make that list, he’ll let us know about it.

#3682. Layoffs, generative AI, and overtime: New study paints bleak picture of 2026 gaming industry

There’s a lot to be excited about in the gaming industry, as new awesome games are constantly being released. But the sad reality is that game development and the industry in general are in a very tough spot.

A new report, GDC’s State of the Game Industry: November 2026, illustrates this unfortunate sentiment and is quite depressing to read through. The top two topics in it are industry layoffs and generative AI, and yeah, that sounds about right when it comes to everybody’s mood inside game dev these days.

Citing people who work in the games industry surveyed from across the world (but mostly the US), GDC also pulled from a pool of 900 laid-off game workers to “dive deeper into their lived experiences.” And here’s the experience: a whopping 68 percent of those laid off from AAA studios were affected in the past year, while 27 percent of them have sent 100 or more job applications since being let go, and 54 percent of them are still unemployed.

And when it comes to sentiment within studios, things are looking and feeling bleak as a result of everything that’s been happening over the past few years, as evidenced by this chart:

A lot of that may have to do with AI usage in the industry, how much it’s being used, and how it’s threatening to take jobs. There’s no good answer for AI in game dev, but most surveyed agree that it should stay in non-creative use only.

But in general, 40 percent of those surveyed say that they use generative AI tools as part of their job, up from 36 percent last year, and 55 percent say that it’s having a negative impact on the industry.

The survey states that “55 percent of game industry professionals think generative AI is having a negative impact on the game industry, unchanged from last year’s 54 percent” and “workers in quality assurance and community support (76 percent) held the most unfavorable views, followed by game design (65 percent), visual and technical arts (65 percent), and audio (57 percent).” Meanwhile, 35% said, “generative AI is having a mixed impact on the game industry, while eight percent said it’s having a positive impact.”

And even with AI, work hours are getting hectic for many: 53 percent said they work over 40 hours weekly, with 13 percent saying they work 51 hours or more, on average, per week.

If you’d like to read the full report, check out the GDC website for all the detailed info.

Certain things are synonymous with Grand Theft Auto - crime, cars, corruption, guns, mayhem and murder. You normally might not expect empathy from a game like GTA 6 with the series' past in mind, then, but Rockstar Games have added "mechanisms" to create empathy anyway.

GTA has always been somewhat of a cynical and comically rude franchise, but it seems Rockstar's now borrowing some lessons from its more grown-up Red Dead Redemption 2. Unrestrained violence and city-wide chaos will still be possible in Leonida - this is a GTA game, after all - but that's not all there is anymore.

Speaking to The Guardian (good spot, IGN), co-studio head Rob Nelson said "crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been." Rockstar is "trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to," so you can still expect the freedom to get into car jams and push passerbys unprovoked (or worse). "[But] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out."

When asked if GTA 6 is encouraging empathy in any way, Nelson agrees: "I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."

GTA 6 notably is the story of two people, Lucia and Jason. In a series full of protagonists who often care very little about anyone outside of their own interests, Lucia and Jason are almost the solar opposite - and quite fittingly, the upcoming game seems to nudge you into behaving differently because of this relationship.

#3680. Hell Let Loose's original developers' Napoleonic-era extraction game, Hunger, gets December early access release, and an open beta this month

Good Fun Corp, the studio made up of the original developers behind Hell Let Loose, has finally announced a release date for its anticipated next project: Hunger. The extraction shooter-slasher game enters early access on Steam on 3rd December, and there's good news if you're eager to try it out before then.

Hunger's first and only open beta has also been announced, taking place 27th-29th November, the weekend prior to its early access launch. Unlike past tests, this one is available for anyone who requests access on Steam.

Though it may appear as yet another extraction shooter on the surface, Hunger offers more complex and intertwined systems than most. For one, combat has a focus on melee with only a few intentionally clunky firearms available. Though this is a PvPvE game, the vs environment side includes the sort of puzzle-solving, questing and dungeon-raiding typical of RPGs. The game's alternate history, plague-ravaged European setting gives it a grimey, steel-and-mud look few games have.

Beyond the in-match experience, Good Fun's ambitions extend to Hunger's MMO-style progression, its hub area with distinct characters and varied playable classes - all of which can be sampled in the upcoming beta.

Hunger just came off a very successful closed beta, which clearly didn't suffer by kicking off right alongside Modern Warfare 4's DMZ early access. Hunger is currently among Steam's most-wishlisted games, with over 700,000 wishlists, according to the developer.

The launch version includes three large maps, six playable characters, and five Mastery trees with more than 100 Masteries to unlock for your characters. Hunger has only been announced for PC so far, but will presumably arrive on consoles following its early access journey.

#3679. Horde PVP character lock in WoW Forever, explained

Having trouble making a Horde character in PvP lately? You're not alone.

If you’ve been eager to hop into World of Warcraft: Forever, create a Horde character, say “lok’tar ogar!” (victory or death!) after an intense PvP match, you’re going to have to wait. There’s an ongoing faction lock on Horde characters in PvP rulesets until further notice.

In a game like WoW, premised on being big on faction warfare, achieving some form of balance across player numbers ensures no one side dominates PvP. And since Forever does have a dedicated mega-realm (ruleset) for PvP players, this faction lock has become a source of frustration.

We’ll look into what we know so far, and update you once it’s finally been lifted.

The faction lock happens when you try to switch over to the PvP ruleset and create a Horde character. Chances are, you’ll be stopped by the game. The error box will state this is due to a “population imbalance.”

If you’ve ever encountered faction restrictions in WoW before, this is a similar situation. Just like the error says, it’s very likely that one faction probably had a lot more players than the other.

“While even the most extreme case in a region is currently at roughly a 55/45 split, that is not as close as we want it to be,” community manager Kaivax said in a post. “Our goal is to bring things as close to a 50/50 faction balance as possible.”

There is no definitive fix for the faction lock as of writing. Some common (albeit unproven) solutions include the following:

There has been no proof that paying for a new account or getting an account boost can fix the lock, so better to stay safe and avoid these. If you want to wait a couple of minutes, avoid using an auto-clicker to be on the safe side.

While waiting, you could also do the following:

Perhaps the most common “answer” to the lock problem is to create a character in the other faction to help balance the population. Unfortunately, this will lock your account’s PvP ruleset to that faction.

If you already have a character in the PvE ruleset, you can hop on there and enjoy its more casual leveling experience. You can still toggle World PvP via the options menu.

Should you want to take the game’s adventuring fantasy more seriously, maybe the RP-PvP ruleset works for you. This just has the added requirement of actually roleplaying your character, so speaking in dialogue, following cues for anything out-of-character, and just fully immersing in Azeroth. Perfect if you want to roleplay your character’s heritage on top of high-stakes PvP.

Character creation restrictions in PvP rulesets weren’t just exclusive to the Horde, however. Blizzard also locked the creation of Alliance characters to some degree, in a bid to ensure character populations across each faction are as balanced as realistically possible.

As such, you might have some difficulty creating characters of a specific faction in a specific region:

Kaivax assured this is temporary and helps the “long-term health of the ruleset,” especially now when guilds are slowly being established.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Other players took to other avenues to explore the faction lock situation as well. While there’s no definite solution aside from waiting, here are other things you should take into account:

There are also other players who have already experienced some version of faction locking before it got widespread. They also posted about it in the Blizzard forums.

However, Yryadorne from customer service clarified that their team isn’t able to unlock this manually.

Some players asked whether trial accounts also affected the count. These are accounts where you could only play for free until Level 20 (with restrictions) without a subscription. Kaivax replied that their testing concluded the trial accounts had nothing to do with the imbalance. They explained that the 55/45 split focused on the “active logged-in population” of players across all levels.

There’s no evidence that creating a lot of trial accounts would fix the faction balance, especially if part of the consideration is that they are “actively” logged in.

Just to be on the safe side, it might be a good idea to check if your Horde lock is related ot any other character creation errors. Blizzard outlined this list, which could be a useful reference:

A lot of players expressed frustration with the inability to create characters in their favored Faction, especially those who want to sink their teeth into PvP in Forever.

The situation has been particularly difficult for players who also want to play with friends of one faction, only to find out it’s currently locked.

One Blizzard forum post even requested some form of compensation, as there’s no proper communication surrounding the faction lock. Other threads also called out the lack of any virtual queue, estimated waiting time, or any way of knowing how long until the restriction is lifted.

The idea of faction-locking isn’t new to Forever, but it certainly came as a shocker to players still getting used to the idea of having one mega-realm to play on.

Things were different in the OG release and Classic, where you could have characters in different realms. Back then, you could only be Horde on one PvP realm and Alliance on another. Faction rules only applied to new players when one faction was starting to crowd a specific realm, so newcomers had to adjust by joining the rival group.

It's been a wild week for fans of the superhero genre. While VisionQuest's finale teased the return of a beloved Marvel hero, moviegoers are still recovering from the change of leadership happening at DC. Between James Gunn being removed as co-CEO of DC Studios and Henry Cavill talking about Superman, fans are feeling a bit frazzled. Although I have another hot take about the ongoing situation.

Back in 2022, James Gunn and Peter Safran were announced at CEOs of DC Studios, and over the past four years they crafted a new shared universe for theaters (and streaming with a HBO Max subscription). While the DCU is still in its infancy, fans are curious about whether the original plan for the first slate of projects, titled Gods and Monsters are still happening. Let's break down the situation, as well as my hot take about Superman.

Earlier this week news broke that both James Gunn and Peter Safran were stepping down from their role as co-CEOs of DC Studios. The pair will be replaced by Former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham, who worked on projects like Iron Man, the first two Avengers movies, and Spider-Man: Homecoming. The news came as a shock, especially so shortly after Clayface hit theaters.

By all accounts it looks like Gunn was fired, but he offered some silver lining when issuing a statement on his Instagram. Part of that statement reads:

But what only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the last. I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that.) I'm always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to short breaks to unwind, and I've stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years.

While Gunn will stop serving as the head of DC on December 1st, he's still got some involvement in the shared universe. He's the director of Man of Tomorrow, which wrapped principal photography back in August. He's also a producer on The Batman: Part Two, which is expected to hit theaters in 2028.

There are countless questions about what'll come next for the DCU, especially since its so early into its life on the screen. Fans are wondering if the original plan for the shared universe will still move forward, or if the studio will opt for yet another reboot. Man of Tomorrow is still coming, but there are some fans hoping that the change of leadership might open the door for Henry Cavill's return as Superman. The 43 year-old actor recently spoke to Inverse and was asked if he'd play the Man of Steel again. He responded with:

Look, there's lots of fantastic storylines. There's always a lot of opportunity. As the pigeon sang to Fievel in An American Tail, 'never say never.' And I buy into that. I’ve had such a wonderful time playing Superman in the past. I would never say never now.

This comment quickly lit up the internet, with some fans who spent years watching the DC movies in order hoping to see Cavill back in the Cape. That includes folks who are still hoping to see Warner Bros. #ResoreTheSnyderVerse and give Zack Snyder his two planned Justice League sequels. I have another perspective, though.

As much as I loved Cavill's take on Superman, I don't think that he should be brought back as the character for the DCU. Instead, I think we should give David Corenswet a fair chance with is portrayal of the DC hero. I loved the hope and kindness he brought to the role in Gunn's Superman, as well as his cameo in Supergirl. He'll once again be taking center stage for Man of Tomorrow, which looks like an exciting crossover featuring various heroes from the newly formed shared universe.

While the studio might be cutting ties with James Gunn, I don't think that should mean the end of Corenswet's tenure as Kal-El. He looks pitch perfect in Superman's costume and trunks, and I loved the kind, punk rock version of the character... especially when compared to the more gritty tone of the SnyderVerse. Give the Hollywood star a chance to cook!

The next upcoming DC movie hitting theaters is Man of Tomorrow on July 9, 2027. Hopefully we get some information about what's coming in the DCU sooner rather than later.

#3677. GTA 6 might be censored in Japan, if the game's smaller install size and lack of "strong sexual content" warning is anything to go by

GTA 6 is finally coming out worldwide next week, putting an end to a 13-year wait and at least one popular meme format, but the highly-anticipated game might look a bit different in Japan.

Now that pre-loading is live for the Rockstar Games mammoth, players across the globe can finally download the game and drool over its icon for the next week or so. But pre-orderers in Japan have noticed that GTA 6's file size comes to about 208GB on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores, versus up to 212GB in other regions.

As reported on by GameSpark and covered by Automaton, the game also received the strictest age rating from the Japanese certification board CERO - "Z" which is recommended for players aged 18 and over - but the listing notably doesn't contain one disclaimer seen in other international ratings.

PEGI and ESRB both warn of the game's "strong sexual content." Curiously, CERO's rating includes no such disclaimer. Together, some fans have taken the lack of "sexual content" disclaimer and smaller file size as signs that GTA 6 might not include some of the risque content we know it'll flaunt elsewhere in the world - based on NSFW leaks and a past rating that already clued us into the fact GTA 6 might be the first GTA to feature full-on sex scenes.

The potential regional censorship isn't too surprising, though, considering how trimmed down GTA 5's Japanese release was at the time. Rockstar had to remove and alter a bunch of GTA 5 scenes to comply with the country's normally strict content guidelines, including Trevor's controversial torture segment and multiple scenes featuring nudity. Baldur's Gate 3, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and many more have been subject to similar restrictions in the past.

Earlier this week, GTA 6 became the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation and Xbox's history. That's also not a huge surprise, either. The juggernaut game's lavish marketing blitz took over London's Selfridges and Rockstar is even hosting an entire music festival starring a couple A-listers.

#3676. How does tanking work in WoW Forever?

Being a tank in WoW: Forever can be serious business. Let's get it right.

Tanks in World of Warcraft: Forever form the bastion of every adventuring party. In front of every DPS who sneaks in a hit and healers who keep everyone alive is a tank who takes on the biggest threats. And unlike other games where getting in front of an enemy is enough, some of WoW‘s toughest dungeons need tanks who focus on both the enemy and their allies.

And finding a tank who knows their way around can be difficult. But if you’re a hopeful adventurer who wants to take their step into tankhood, we’ll walk you through the basics. So grab your shield, prep your auras, and let’s pull mobs.

Threat is the most important term in any tank’s vocabulary, since every other tanking concept stems from it. “Threat” is something you generate that determines how likely an NPC is to get aggressive towards you. When an enemy starts attacking you, you’ve generated enough Threat for them to get aggro (aggressive).

No in-game setting reveals how much threat someone generates, and we’ve often had to rely on add-ons (we’ll get to that later) to determine that number. Based on Classic data, Threat usually works like this:

Tanks who attack first secure the Threat. But other party members can easily bypass your Threat level if their damage and heals are absurdly high, usually from DPS and healers. So tanks have to “steal” that Threat back through special abilities. This is where tanks come in with Taunts.

These are abilities that bypass current Threat levels entirely, so NPCs who are affected are forced to attack the caster (tank) instead. Most Taunts last a short while, so tanks usually start rotations with them or whenever tanks feel they need to yoink attention back from mobs. All tanking Classes have Taunts or some other way of stealing aggro back.

Tanks share common qualities even in MMOs. More often than not, they’re the bulkiest units of any party. They’re built to hold the front line, take punishment, and give the rest of the team enough time to finish the fight.

These principles still apply when building a tank in Forever, and these stats are also your ideal targets when pursuing gear in dungeons or crafting them through Professions:

The only stats where these differ would be based on your chosen tanking Class, as some of them have additional stats you should take note of.

The big tl;dr for tanks is to rush to a mob, attack all of them, and use Taunts to keep them away from the party. But that’s just the beginning. Your tank must maintain this momentum regardless of what happens on the battlefield, and these techniques help you adjust to the most common situations:

The ideal scenario in any dungeon is to go to a cluster of mobs, pull them from their general location, and kill them. If you’re with an experienced group, they’d tell you to go to maybe three mob spots at once, pull all of them, and let the team handle it. Both scenarios are correct, but ideally you’d want to take it slow.

Pings are in the game for a reason. Mark your priority target with a skull and a secondary one with a cross. That ensures everyone knows who you plan to focus on stealing Threat from, and they can attack accordingly. Normally, you’d want to target spellcasters first.

When you rush to the mob and start attacking, try not to have your party behind you. Instead, move slowly so the mob follows your general direction until their backs are on the rest of your party. Keep on Taunting throughout the process, so even if Rogues dish out enough DPS to steal Threat, you can force their attention on you. This also ensures your party isn’t being harassed by some stray mob.

As a tank, you likely have spells and abilities that help you absorb damage or resist attacks. Don’t use those buffs all at once. Find rotations where there’s a balance of proccing buffs, attacking mobs, refreshing buffs, and doing it again. If you have instant blocks, save them for critical moments or incorporate them in your rotations.

Your DPS have crowd control abilities to “control” the flow of enemies, and you should take advantage of that. When your damage-dealers stun or slow opponents (Mages with sheep, Rogues with sap, Hunters with traps), try to damage the non-controlled mobs first. Then alternate.

Healers have it tough, as they can generate so much Threat even when they’re not attacking. As a tank, your main priority is to keep the healer alive, since they keep everyone else alive. Ideally, you’d pause if the healer is out of mana so they can recover. A great way to know is to turn on power bars in your party so you can track their resources.

Besides healers, DPS can get ridiculously squishy as their damage numbers can get off the charts. Now a DPS isn’t as useful to the party if they end up soloing mobs or a boss with no one to give backup. Remind your DPS to stay behind mobs at all times, or pull mobs in such a way that they’re facing away from the DPS. Make it a habit to mark your targets, so everyone knows where to focus their attack and who you’re stealing Threat from.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Tanking in WoW: Forever is usually reserved for a select number of Classes with specs tailored for the role. As tanking relies heavily on defense, the Classes that can reliably tank are often the ones that can handle getting hit, can heal themselves after getting hit, or annoy the enemy enough to always stay aggro’d:

Warriors depend on Rage, which they get from hitting and being hit. Their Protection spec is mostly built for tanking, and they have some of the strongest Threat-stealing abilities in the game. Base Warrior alone gets bonus Threat from Defensive Stance and can steal Threat from single targets (Shield Slam, Sunder Armor), mobs (Taunt), and in emergencies (Mocking Blow, Challenging Shout).

They also have nifty tools in their arsenal, such as an early-game interrupt (Shield Bash) and a damage debuff (Demoralizing Shout), among other attacks that often punish opponents.

Paladins are part magic-users, so they also rely on Mana to cast spells. Their Righteous Fury gets them more Threat as they use their toolkit. And just like other tanks, they have their fair share of taunts for single-target (Holy Strike, Seal of Fury and Judgment), and mobs (Consecration).

However, Paladins set themselves apart for their party-wide buffs that reduce damage (Devotion Aura) and give a 10% overall stat boost (Blessing of Kings). Protection is their main tanking spec, but you can also go for Holy if you want to be a sub-healer.

Druids are perhaps the most versatile Class in Forever due to their many forms, and they still have potent heals even as tanks. Their Bear Form is what gets the most threat, and Druids have many mob-based taunts (Challenging Roar, Growl, Swipe) as well. Feral is their main tanking spec, which grants them a decent single-target taunt (Primal Bite). When transformed, Rage is also their primary resource, and it can facilitate vicious combos.

Aside from tanking, Druids can become competent emergency healers. They have access to an instant-cast heal-over-time (Rejuvenation), an instant heal that is upgradeable to an HoT (Regrowth), and a decent AOE (Wild Growth),

Earlier this year, during the Overwatch Spotlight in which Team 4 promised a different approach to managing the live service game, 10 heroes were teased. Five were released straight away, with Sierra, Shion, D.Mon, and Doctrine all being added to the game in subsequent seasons. This has left just one hero for the last season of the year, who also just so happened to be the hero I was most excited about back when the Spotlight was released.

But good things come to those who wait, and now after the better part of a year we finally know more about this final hero. His character design was shown at BlizzCon, which showed him to be omnic detective (my hype was well placed), but now we also know that he'll be joining the DPS class in season 6, although that wasn't always the plan.

"Back at Spotlight—I forget who I was talking to—we said we were going to do a support in season 6," associate game director Alec Dawson said during a stream with Flats and Emongg. "And originally that was the plan. But as things developed as the hero developed, as we got to mechanics, how they matched with the aesthetic, how they matched with who the hero is supposed to be," things changed. The decision was ultimately taken to switch him to the DPS role. "I don't know what else I'm allowed to say," Dawson adds. "I'll let Aaron [Keller, game director] say anything else."

"We'll just spill it all," Keller says, and that he does. "Megan just slacked that we've said enough but there's a couple of other things that I want to say about him. One of the cool things about this, so there was like a bit of a pivot on Hudson (accidentally leaks his name), oh whoops." Well there it is folks: the omnic detective is called Hudson, a cool name for a cool dude, it all checks out.

Hudson's Role Change Explained in #Overwatch 🔎 He was initially planned as a Support hero, but as development progressed, the team realized the core mechanic people loved most fit the DPS role better. The hero set record scores in research groups. https://t.co/VxTMpsPLUrNovember 13, 2026

As a support main I am a little sad to hear about this change to DPS, but seeing as Team 4 explained how they "leaned into the things we loved the most about this hero and it definitely fit DPS a lot better", I'm happy with the change. I'll just have to put support aside for a couple of months, because there's no way I'm missing out on this hero.

This isn't just because he looks cool; according to Keller, Hudson is the most popular hero to-date among their internal and external testers: "We're always testing stuff and we have a user research group here and we'll bring in external players and stuff like that, and this hero by far got the highest scores of any hero that we've tested with these groups. I think he's so much fun."

To put this into perspective, the second most popular hero among testers within the last few years is Juno; a hero I would consider to be one of the best in recent Overwatch history. Her kit is fun, intuitive, and gels with her character design. So if that's the bar Hudson has beaten then my excitement is yet again very well placed. Oh, and Dawson says "he has a very fun accent", which really seals the deal for me.

#3674. Don't expect more information on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel "for some time," Bethesda says

After Bethesda formally named The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel earlier this month, some series fans were hopeful that more news wasn't far behind. Skyrim is 15 years old today (11th November) after all, but Bethesda Game Studios has since dashed those hopes into oblivion.

In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

"Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any big announcements tomorrow," the social media account wrote. "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything new on Sentinel for some time."

The Elder Scrolls fans have already been waiting for the series' next mainline follow-up for, erm, also quite some time. Specifically, Skyrim came out in 2011, The Elder Scrolls 6's first reveal trailer reared its head in 2018, and BGS' Starfield took to the stars in 2023 - a wait so long that it had even the most faithful among us questioning if a new Elder Scrolls could ever recapture the series' magic.

So, there you have it - don't expect to see or hear about Sentinel anytime soon. Better yet, lock it up in some corner of your brain and be pleasantly surprised when it does miraculously reappear in 20XX.

In the meantime, Bethesda isn't letting Skyrim's 15th anniversary go by without a few celebrations. For one, the seminal role-playing game is deeply discounted on all platforms, in the very unlikely scenario you haven't tried it out yet.

The Elder Scrolls Online Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim is also joining the festivities by adding the Greymoor Chapter into the base game for free, giving everyone access to a few famous Skyrim locales and more. A brand-new, separate Golden Pursuit campaign will let you earn some Skyrim-centric goodies up until 2nd December, as well.

#3672. Just how many games were born out of this silly Japanese commercial from 1986?

Does your mind get blown when you find out that the origin story of something you love is nothing like you pictured it? Like, how wild would it be to learn that the Final Fantasy series was inspired by a beverage commercial? Well, buckle up.

One of the most famous pieces of Final Fantasy trivia says SquareSoft picked that name because the company was in dire straits, knew it would be their last game, and wanted to go out with a bang. Cool story, bro; too bad it’s bunk. The original Japanese name for Final Fantasy actually translated to something closer to Fighting Fantasy in English, which immediately proves that whole story is rubbish. Also, why would a company expect to close after making a great, successful game? Final Fantasy wasn’t made in 2026, after all.

I’m reasonably well-versed in video game history, knowledgeable enough to know that many of the game development tales we’ve been hearing throughout the decades are completely fabricated, but a lot about Final Fantasy‘s origins remains a mystery, so I was pretty surprised when I stumbled upon a post on Bluesky putting forward the idea that a lot of Final Fantasy was actually inspired by a pretty silly energy drink commercial, starring Cindy Crawford, where the supermodel dons a set of armor to seemingly battle it out with an invisible enemy.

It's funny how much Final Fantasy 1 owes to this 1986 Japanese Cindy Crawford Pocari Sweat ad, art directed by Moebius

No offense to Crawford, who’s not really a fantasy knight, but her sword moves are so stiff they seem straight out of an old game. All meanness aside, even if that armor heavily resembles the outfits of Yoshitaka Amano’s era, it’s hard to tell whether the commercial itself inspired the people behind the popular RPG series. Still, we do know the commercial’s art direction was handled by the late French comic book artist Jean Giraud, aka Moebius, who is one of the greatest names in manga and anime. To give you an idea, the creators of Akira, Ghost in the Shell, and many of Studio Ghibli’s works cite Moebius as a main source of inspiration. I find it incredibly interesting that, even if unintentionally, his stint with commercials might’ve proved equally inspiring to a completely different type of media.

So, if you’re of the mind that the French completely ripped off Final Fantasy and Japanese RPGs to make Expedition 33, well, then think again, as they might’ve just been reaping what they’d sowed over 30 years ago.

To make matters even more interesting, the same thread revealed that Cindy Crawford’s adventure with games wasn’t over after that commercial, as she’d go on to model for none other than Samus Aran in an early iteration of Metroid Prime.

I had no idea about any of this. Regardless, did the aesthetics of Final Fantasy really originate from the commercial for a drink with a name as dumb as “Pocari Sweat”? I don’t know. I do know, however, that in the 2000s, SquareSoft made an actual soda commercial starring the characters of the most nostalgia-bait-y of all Final Fantasy games, so there’s some food for thought.

There’s no way of knowing for sure, just like you can’t count just how many other cool pieces of media might’ve gotten inspiration out of such a then-peculiar ad. What I do know for sure, however, is that Final Fantasy fans sure do like a good fan theory, even ones that have been thoroughly debunked by the game’s creators—which is not the case with this one—so good luck getting this one out of your heads whenever you see classic Final Fantasy popping up anywhere.
